can: Consigo falar do que sei e do que consegui fazer, descrever como me sinto com adjetivos -ed e -ing, e pedir ou oferecer ajuda.

lessons.title: Vocabulário
lessons.goal: Aprender o vocabulário da unidade: Adjetivos -ed x -ing (bored x boring, tired x tiring, confused x confusing).

aula.label: Regra
aula.text: adjetivo em **-ed** diz como a pessoa se sente. Adjetivo em **-ing** diz o que causa esse sentimento.
*I'm bored. The film is boring.* Cuidado: *He's boring* quer dizer "ele é chato", e *He's bored* quer dizer "ele está entediado".

items: "I'm boring in this meeting." O certo é **I'm bored.**
"The movie was interested." O certo é **The movie was interesting.**
"I'm excited with the trip." O certo é excited **about** the trip.

acc: I am bored in this meeting

exercises.prompt: Football isn't interesting to me. I'm not ___ in football.

lessons.title: Can, could e be able to
lessons.goal: Dominar a gramática da unidade: can / can't, could / couldn't, be able to (vários tempos).

head: Forma
Uso
Exemplo
rows: I can swim. I can't come tomorrow.
habilidade geral no passado; pedido educado
I could swim when I was five. Could you help me?
conseguir fazer algo específico, uma vez
I was able to fix the car yesterday.
I won't be able to come. I'd like to be able to play the guitar.

aula.label: Dica
aula.text: habilidade geral no passado = *could*. Um êxito específico = *was able to*. Na negativa, *couldn't* serve para os dois.

items: "I can to swim." O certo é **I can swim.**
"I don't can." O certo é **I can't.**
"I will can go." O certo é **I'll be able to go.**

exercises.prompt: I ___ swim when I was four.
I'm sorry, I ___ come on Saturday.
After three tries, I finally ___ ___ ___ open the door.
I will can help you tomorrow.
acc: I'll be able to help you tomorrow
I will be able to help you tomorrow

exercises.prompt: I'd love to ___ ___ ___ play the guitar.

head: Situação
Frases
rows: Can you help me with...? / Could you give me a hand? / I need some help with...
Can I help you? / Do you need a hand? / Shall I carry that for you? / Let me help you.
Yes, please. / That would be great. / Thanks, that's very kind.
No, thanks, I'm fine. / It's OK, I can manage.
Thanks a lot. / I really appreciate it. / Any time.

items: "Can you help me to the homework?" O certo é help me **with**.
"I appreciate" sozinho. O certo é **I appreciate it.**
